strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real deployment challenges of state-of-the-art ColPali models (10MB per document, high latency)
Impressive efficiency-quality tradeoffs: achieves 14× speedup and 54× memory reduction compared to Llama-Nemo while maintaining comparable NDCG@5 (62.7 vs 62.9)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 9 model pairs, 8 hybrid baselines, extensive ablations (Tables 14-17), comparison to cross-encoder reranking
Architecture-agnostic and practical: works with single/multi-vector retrievers, adds only 60-350ms latency, requires no model retraining
Clear presentation and reproducibility: well-written paper with effective visualizations, detailed implementation appendices, promised code release
Robust to design choices: ablations show consistent performance across loss functions (KL, Jensen-Shannon), candidate pool policies, and role assignments
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: combines known techniques (test-time optimization, KL divergence minimization) in straightforward manner; insufficient insight into why this specific combination is effective

Concerning generalization on ViDoRe 1: shows essentially zero improvement (-0.1% average, Table 7), suggesting method may not help when base models already perform well; raises questions about real-world applicability
Requires supervised hyperparameter tuning: demands 10% in-domain development set (not zero-shot); hyperparameters (α, T) appear dataset-dependent, limiting applicability to new domains
Lacks theoretical justification: explicitly empirical focus; no convergence analysis, theoretical guarantees, or principled explanation for when GQR should help; authors acknowledge this limitation
Counterintuitive phenomenon unexplored: text retrievers significantly underperform ColPali (46.8-55.3 vs 60-63 NDCG@5) yet provide helpful guidance; source of complementarity is unexplained
Non-trivial latency overhead: still 2.5× slower than base Colnomic (181ms vs 116ms); 60-350ms overhead may not justify added complexity in latency-sensitive applications
Mixed results and failure modes: scattered negative results (Table 1: -2.4, -0.4) with limited investigation; gains range from +0.3 to +2.8 across settings without systematic characterization

Loss function insensitivity concerning: Table 16 shows different objectives (KL variants, Jensen-Shannon) produce similar results, raising questions about whether method is learning specific to the objective

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical impact: demonstrates 14× latency reduction and 54× memory savings compared to LLAMA-NEMORETRIEVER while achieving competitive performance
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 3 established benchmarks (ViDoRe 1/2/3), 9 model pairs, both tuned and zero-shot settings, thorough ablations on hyperparameters and design choices
Consistent improvements across all evaluated hybrid methods: GQR achieves 3.9% average gain on ViDoRe 2, outperforming tuned score aggregation (3.4%) and ranking fusion methods
Architecture-agnostic approach applicable to both single- and multi-vector embeddings, with clear algorithmic description and promised code release for reproducibility
Insightful analysis: hyperparameter investigation reveals interpretable tradeoffs, per-query dynamics demonstrate distinctness from score aggregation, latency breakdown quantifies optimization costs
Practical Pareto frontier improvements: clearly demonstrates efficiency-performance tradeoffs across multiple models with detailed latency/memory measurements
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution is adapting existing test-time query optimization (Yu et al. 2021, Sung et al. 2023) by replacing cross-encoder with bi-encoder guidance—incremental rather than transformative

Modest empirical gains on strongest baselines: LLAMA-NEMORETRIEVER (63.0→65.2, +2.2), COLNOMIC-7B (60.3→63.1, +2.8); improvements diminish when compared to tuned baselines (3.9% vs 3.4% for tuned Score Aggregation)

Lacks theoretical justification: unclear why KL(p_avg||p₁) is optimal when Table 18 shows Jensen-Shannon and KL(p₂||p₁) perform 'similarly well'; consensus distribution (simple 0.5 weighting) appears arbitrary without learned alternatives tested

Hyperparameter sensitivity without strong zero-shot generalization: 2 hyperparameters (α, T) with high variance (Figure 4); zero-shot ViDoRe 3 results only marginally exceed tuned baselines (2.89% vs 2.66%), suggesting limited domain generalization

Evaluation limited to visual document retrieval: no evidence of applicability to dense retrieval, QA, e-commerce or other domains; ViDoRe 1 saturated (90+ on many subsets) limiting utility; zero-shot uses ViDoRe 2 hyperparameters

Insufficient analysis of failure modes and complementary retriever quality impact: unexplained degradation in some model pairs (e.g., +0.7 gain on ESG Human for Colnomic+Qwen3); no systematic investigation of when/why GQR works
Non-trivial latency overhead masked by framing: 50-100ms optimization cost represents 56% latency increase for Colnomic (115.98→181.21ms), potentially problematic for latency-sensitive applications

Experimental design inconsistencies: text models use Docling OCR (variable quality) on ViDoRe 1/2 while vision models use images; ViDoRe 3 uses markdown for text models but images for vision models—different content modalities confound comparisons
Missing statistical significance testing and incomplete baseline comparisons: marginal improvements over tuned Score Aggregation with comparable standard deviations lack statistical validation
Insufficient intuition for practitioners: unclear guidance on when to apply GQR, how complementary retriever quality affects performance, or why certain model pairs underperform
